## Policy

### Scope of Policy

This Clinical Policy Bulletin addresses influenza vaccines, including those for avian influenza A viruses or bird flu.

1. ### Medical Necessity

   Aetna considers the following U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved influenza vaccines medically necessary according to the best available evidence and recommendations of leading medical organizations (e.g., Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's [CDC] Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices [ACIP], American College of Physicians [ACP], American Academy of Pediatrics [AAP], Infectious Diseases Society of America [IDSA]):

   1. FDA-approved standard or preservative-free trivalent influenza injectables (e.g., Afluria, Fluarix, Flucelvax, Fluzone) for members 6 months of age or older; or
   2. FDA-approved standard or preservative-free trivalent influenza injectable (e.g., Flublok) for members 9 years of age or older; or
   3. FDA-approved preservative-free trivalent influenza injectable (e.g., Fluad, Fluzone High-Dose) for members 65 years of age and older; or
   4. FDA-approved mRNA trivalent influenza injectable (mFLUSIVA) for members 50 years of age or older; or
   5. FDA-approved trivalent intranasal vaccine (e.g., FluMist) for members aged 2 through 49 years of age. Notes: The CDC recommendation for FluMist includes self- or caregiver administration. The CDC does not recommend use in individuals who are pregnant, immunocompromised, or have certain medical conditions (e.g., asthma).

   #### Notes on avian influenza A vaccination:

   Vaccines targeting avian influenza A (H5N1) viruses have been approved by the U.S. FDA for use in persons at increased risk of exposure; however, these vaccines are not routinely available or recommended for the general U.S. population. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services maintains preparedness activities through the National Pre-Pandemic Influenza Vaccine Stockpile (NPIVS) program, which supports development and stockpiling of vaccines against novel influenza A viruses, including H5N1. The CDC continues to monitor avian influenza activity and associated human exposures. As of the most recent CDC updates, the public health risk to the general population remains low, and the CDC's ACIP has not issued recommendations for routine H5N1 vaccination of the general public (CDC, 2025a).
2. ### Related Policies

## Background

Influenza ("the flu") is a contagious respiratory illness caused by viruses that infect the nose, throat, and sometimes the lungs. Influenza can cause mild to severe illness, and at times can lead to death. Symptoms, which may appear suddenly, include fever, chills, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, muscle or body aches, headaches, and fatigue. It is important to note that not everyone with the flu will have a fever. In addition, some people may have vomiting and diarrhea, though this is more common in children than adults. Most experts believe that flu viruses spread mainly by tiny droplets made when people infected with the flu cough, sneeze or talk. Less often, a person might get the flu from contact with a contaminated surface or object and subsequently touch their own mouth, nose, or possibly their eyes. # Memorandum From the Physician to the President on the President's Comprehensive Follow-Up Evaluation at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center

PHYSICIAN TO THE PRESIDENT  
THE WHITE HOUSE

MEMORANDUM

October 10, 2025

TO: KAROLINE LEAVITT, WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY

FROM: SEAN P. BARBABELLA, D.O.  
PHYSICIAN TO THE PRESIDENT  
CAPTAIN, U.S. NAVY

SUBJECT: President Donald J. Trump Completes Comprehensive Follow-Up Evaluation at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

President Donald J. Trump successfully completed a scheduled follow-up evaluation today at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center. The visit was part of his ongoing health maintenance plan and included advanced imaging, laboratory testing, and preventive health assessments conducted by a multidisciplinary team of specialists. These evaluations were performed in coordination with leading academic and medical consultants to ensure optimal cardiovascular health and continued wellness.

Comprehensive laboratory studies performed in conjunction with the visit were exceptional, including stable metabolic, hematologic, and cardiac parameters.

In preparation for upcoming international travel, President Trump also received preventive health screenings and immunizations, including annual influenza and updated COVID-19 booster vaccinations.

President Trump continues to demonstrate excellent overall health. His cardiac age-a validated measure of cardiovascular vitality via ECG-was found to be approximately 14 years younger than his chronological age. He continues to maintain a demanding daily schedule without restriction.

SUMMARY: President Donald J. Trump remains in exceptional health, exhibiting strong cardiovascular, pulmonary, neurological, and physical performance.
